Honeywell Announces $600 Million Capital Raise For Quantinuum at $10B Pre-Money Equity Valuation to Advance Quantum Computing at Scale

September 4, 2025

Source: Honeywell

Charlotte, N.C., September 4th, 2025 — Honeywell today announced an approximately $600 million equity capital raise for Quantinuum, developer of the world’s highest-performing quantum computer, at a pre-money equity valuation of $10 billion. 

Quanta Computer, NVentures (NVIDIA’s venture capital arm) and QED Investors have joined existing shareholders JPMorganChase, Mitsui, Amgen, Cambridge Quantum Holdings, Serendipity Capital and Honeywell — all of whom have reinvested in this round. The round also includes participation from new investors MESH and Korea Investment Partners.

This capital raise will support Quantinuum’s advancement of quantum computing at scale, which includes continued progress toward the upcoming launch of Helios, the company’s next generation quantum computing system that is expected to launch this year. It will also support Quantinuum’s path to becoming the first to perform universal fault-tolerant computing. 

A full-stack quantum computing provider, Quantinuum is accelerating commercially useful quantum computing with commercially available quantum computers that are the undisputed leaders in performance. Along with some of the most used developer tools and end-applications such as InQuanto, the company’s solutions are driving breakthrough scientific discoveries, economic growth and sustainable development.  

Quantinuum continues increasing its commercial momentum and earning global recognition. The company will work with NVIDIA as a founding collaborator on breakthroughs at the NVIDIA Accelerated Quantum Research Center.  Additionally, Quantinuum has entered strategic partnerships aimed at innovative quantum computing solutions that will expand the capabilities of classical artificial intelligence and realize next-generation technologies. Quantinuum recently announced partnerships and collaborations with RIKEN, SoftBank Corp., Infineon and STFC Hartree Center, as well as expansions into New Mexico, Qatar and Singapore. 

The company’s collaborations collectively provide substantial investment, accelerating research and development, product development, scaling manufacturing capabilities, securing supply chains and fostering the overall growth of the quantum technologies industry. For example, the company’s Joint Venture in Qatar was selected to deliver advanced quantum computing infrastructure and solutions to the region as part of Qatar’s $1 billion investment over the next decade. In Singapore, Quantinuum is enabling access to the company’s advanced quantum computer, and to explore and collaborate on quantum use cases, focusing on computational biology.    

Vimal Kapur, Chairman and CEO of Honeywell:
“Quantinuum continues to meet and exceed our stated objectives — strategically, technically and commercially. We have complete confidence in Quantinuum’s ability to continue to lead the quantum revolution and create long-term value for its investors and customers.”

Scot Baldry, Chief Technology Officer of JPMorganChase:
“We have seen firsthand the transformative potential of Quantinuum’s technology. We are looking forward to continuing our work together to help accelerate innovation and move closer toward solving real-world problems through quantum applications.”

Dr. Rajeeb Hazra, President & CEO of Quantinuum: 
“We are proud to partner with investors who share deep conviction in our vision for the future of quantum and AI. With the continued support of our customers and supply chain partners, this new funding will further extend our leadership, accelerate our roadmap and strengthen the entire quantum ecosystem.”

J.P. Morgan Securities LLC served as exclusive placement agent to Quantinuum in connection with the financing. Freshfields LLP acted as external legal counsel.

Honeywell is an integrated operating company serving a broad range of industries and geographies around the world. Our business is aligned with three powerful megatrends – automation, the future of aviation and energy transition – underpinned by our Honeywell Accelerator operating system and Honeywell Forge IoT platform. As a trusted partner, we help organizations solve the world's toughest, most complex challenges, providing actionable solutions and innovations through our Aerospace Technologies, Industrial Automation, Building Automation and Energy and Sustainability Solutions business segments that help make the world smarter, safer, as well as more secure and sustainable. November 10, 2026
Quantinuum and RIKEN Expand Partnership to Accelerate the Commercialization of Quantum-AI Hybrid Supercomputing in Japan
  • Completed upgrade of Quantinuum’s Reimei quantum computer to its H2 system establishes RIKEN’s hybrid quantum-supercomputing platform as the most capable of its kind in the world and creates a pathway to expand research across electronics, energy and life sciences.
  • Quantinuum and RIKEN will build upon this pioneering computing architecture to develop a fault-tolerant “Made with Japan” quantum computer to extend Japan’s long-term quantum leadership.
  • To further accelerate commercial adoption of quantum-AI hybrid supercomputing in Japan, the partners will collaborate with SoftBank Corp. to develop a path to connect quantum computers directly with AI data centers.

TOKYO — November 10, 2026 — Quantinuum (NASDAQ: QNT), a leading full-stack quantum computing company, and RIKEN, Japan’s leading national comprehensive research institute, today announced an expanded partnership to advance quantum-AI hybrid supercomputing in Japan. Following a significant upgrade to Quantinuum’s Reimei quantum computer at RIKEN, the partners will pursue more advanced scientific and industrial applications, work with Japanese universities and suppliers toward the development of a “Made with Japan” fault-tolerant quantum computer, and collaborate with SoftBank Corp. to explore the connection of quantum computer with AI data centers in Japan.

Quantinuum’s quantum computer, Reimei, installed at RIKEN, has successfully completed its upgrade to System Model H2. Reimei is operated as part of the JHPC-quantum project, funded by NEDO. This upgrade further enhances the capabilities of the project's quantum–HPC hybrid computing platform and enables researchers to investigate more complex quantum systems that are increasingly difficult to simulate using classical computing alone, broadening the scientific problems they can explore.

Quantinuum and RIKEN will use the upgraded platform to combine quantum computing, supercomputing and AI in support of use case development across electronics, energy and life sciences. Building on their years-long collaboration, the partners will also draw on their experience integrating and operating Reimei to inform the development of a fault-tolerant “Made with Japan” quantum computer.

“Japan’s quantum ambitions require advanced capabilities today and a sustained commitment to developing what comes next,” said Dr. Rajeeb Hazra, Quantinuum CEO. “The upgrade to Reimei expands what we can explore with RIKEN across electronics, energy and life sciences. Together, we are building on this work to develop a fault-tolerant quantum computer with Japanese universities and suppliers, while exploring with SoftBank how these capabilities can become accessible to industry through Japan’s AI data centers.”

Two research projects that have begun operations on Reimei before the public launch of its services illustrate how Quantinuum and RIKEN are leveraging the hybrid platforms upgraded capabilities to push the frontiers of scientific discovery:

  • Quantum-AI for materials simulation: The partners are using RIKEN’s JHPC-quantum GPU supercomputer, ROQUO, to train an AI model on Reimei-generated quantum data for magnetism simulations. Preliminary results suggest the model can make more accurate predictions than AI models trained on classical simulations alone and more precise predictions than the quantum computer itself. Understanding magnetism at the atomic level could inform the development of materials for next-generation technologies such as ultra-high-field MRI and smart power grids.
  • Quantum-AI for biomolecular simulation: The partners are combining Reimei, RIKEN’s Fugaku supercomputer, and NVIDIA’s evolutionary AI agent running on ROQUO to simulate a complex photoactive biomolecule, targeting unprecedented scale and detail. Better understanding of how biomolecules respond to light could inform the design of more efficient solar cells among other industrial opportunities that could arise from advances in biomolecular engineering.

This research supports RIKEN’s AI for Science initiative and aligns with U.S.-Japan efforts to advance AI-driven discovery, including a planned $1 billion partnership under the U.S. Genesis Mission.

“With the upgraded Reimei quantum computer, we will be able to tackle more complex and larger-scale scientific problems that were difficult to address with the previous H1 system, further advancing quantum–HPC hybrid computing through our ongoing JHPC-quantum project,” said Dr. Mitsuhisa Sato, Division Director, Quantum-HPC Hybrid Platform Division, RIKEN Center for Computational Science (R-CCS). “Furthermore, the newly signed Memorandum of Understanding will pave the way for expanding our research into the use of quantum computing for AI for Science, a key initiative being promoted by RIKEN.”

The partners’ joint research and development toward a “Made with Japan” fault-tolerant quantum computer will involve Japanese universities and domestic components suppliers. This “Made with Japan” effort will combine Quantinuum’s quantum technology with domestic research and manufacturing expertise, drawing on lessons from integrating and operating Reimei at RIKEN.

Under a separate agreement, Quantinuum, RIKEN and SoftBank will explore how quantum computing can be connected directly with AI data centers in Japan. The partners will assess infrastructure readiness and examine how connected systems could support commercial quantum-AI hybrid computing services, broadening access beyond the research community.

“Japan has established a strong foundation for hybrid quantum-HPC computing through the NEDO-supported JHPC-quantum project,” said Takenori Kobayashi, Vice President, Head of Product Research & Development Division at SoftBank Corp. “Our responsibility is to turn these achievements into industrial value. Together with RIKEN and Quantinuum, we aim to advance a Quantum AI Datacenter that connects quantum computing with AI and HPC, making these capabilities accessible to businesses across Japan.”

Learn more about the expanded joint Quantinuum-RIKEN research available here.

Research Support

This project is supported by New Energy and Industrial Technology Development Organization (NEDO), an organization under the jurisdiction of Japan's Ministry of Economy, Trade and Industry (METI)'s "Research and Development of Quantum-Supercomputers Hybrid Platform for Exploration of Uncharted Computable Capabilities" (Project Leader: Mitsuhisa Sato) as part of the "Project for Research and Development of Enhanced Infrastructures for Post 5G Information and Communications Systems (JPNP20017)."

About RIKEN

RIKEN, a National Research and Development Agency, is Japan’s leading national comprehensive research institution renowned for high-quality research in a diverse range of scientific disciplines. Founded in 1917, initially as a private research foundation, RIKEN has grown rapidly in size and scope, today encompassing a network of world-class research centers and institutes across Japan. To learn more, please visit https://www.riken.jp/en

About SoftBank Corp.

Guided by the SoftBank Group’s corporate philosophy, “Information Revolution – Happiness for everyone,” SoftBank Corp. (TOKYO: 9434) operates telecommunications and IT businesses in Japan and globally. Building on its strong business foundation, SoftBank Corp. is aiming to activate the potential of AI across its businesses and drive implementation in line with its “Activate AI for Society” growth strategy. While further growing its telecom business, SoftBank is expanding its AI computing infrastructure and AI and Cloud service businesses with the aim of becoming a provider of Next-generation Social Infrastructure. To learn more, please visit https://www.softbank.jp/en/corp.

About Quantinuum

Quantinuum (NASDAQ: QNT) is a leading quantum computing company offering a full-stack platform designed to make quantum computing deployable in real-world environments. The company has commercially deployed multiple generations of trapped-ion based quantum systems built on the well-established QCCD architecture, which it has implemented with novel designs and capabilities to achieve the industry’s highest accuracy levels based on average two-qubit gate fidelity. Quantinuum has active engagements with market leaders across pharmaceuticals, material science, financial services, and government and industrial markets, as well as academic and research institutions globally. The company has a global workforce of approximately 800 employees, including top scientists and researchers. Over 70% of its technology team holds PhDs or Master’s degrees. Quantinuum’s headquarters is in Broomfield, Colorado, with additional facilities across the United States, United Kingdom, Germany, Japan, Qatar, and Singapore. For more information, please visit www.quantinuum.com.

November 5, 2026
Quantinuum Reports Third Quarter 2026 Results and Raises Full-Year Revenue Outlook
  • Third-Quarter Revenue Grew 233% Year-Over-Year; Raised FY2026 Revenue Outlook
  • Extended Fault-Tolerance Industry Leadership with Back-to-Back World Records, Validating Most Credible Path to Universal, Fault-Tolerant Quantum Computing
  • Announced Nexus Roadmap Through Apollo; Platform Adoption Grew Nearly 20% Quarter-Over-Quarter and Job Submissions Increased Tenfold Year-Over-Year for the 12 Months Ended August 2026
  • Secured Largest Cloud Agreement in Company History, Including Multi-Year Committed Full-Stack Access Through Apollo
  • Expanded Enterprise Reach Through Leading Hyperscaler Agreement and Oracle Beta Launch

Quantinuum Inc. (Nasdaq: QNT) (the “Company”), a leading full-stack quantum computing company, today announced financial results for the third quarter ended September 30, 2026.  
“In the third-quarter, we extended our technology leadership in the critical area of fault-tolerance, added to our customer base, and expanded our routes to market,” said Rajeeb Hazra, President and Chief Executive Officer of Quantinuum. “This accelerated momentum is supporting our raised revenue outlook for 2026 and giving us more confidence than ever in the opportunity in front of us.”

Third Quarter 2026 Financial Highlights

  • Revenue was $9.1 million, an increase of 233% year-over-year, compared with $2.7 million in the prior-year period.  
  • GAAP gross margin was 33.3%, compared with (43.5%) the prior-year period.
  • Adjusted gross margin was 74.6%, up 853 basis points versus the prior-year period.
  • Adjusted EBITDA loss was $80 million, compared with a loss of $45 million in the prior-year period.  
  • GAAP net loss was $118 million, compared with a net loss of $52 million in the prior-year period.
  • GAAP net loss per share attributable to Class A common stockholders was $0.46.  
  • Adjusted net loss per share was $0.29.
  • Cash & cash equivalents were $1.94 billion as of September 30, 2026.  

Adjusted EBITDA, Adjusted Gross Margin and Adjusted net loss per share are non-GAAP financial measures defined under “Non-GAAP Financial Measures.” For a reconciliation of these non-GAAP financial measures to the most directly comparable GAAP financial measures, refer to the Appendix tables at the end of this press release.

Third Quarter and Recent Business Highlights

Commercial Highlights:

  • Signed the largest cloud agreement in Company history, securing a multi-year extension with a leading global financial institution that includes committed access through Apollo and Nexus.
  • Signed with another top 5 global pharmaceuticals company on applying quantum computing and AI to cancer-therapy materials that offer the potential to accelerate drug development and enable more effective treatments.  
  • Signed agreement with GE Vernova to advance application development in superconducting materials.
  • Signed deal with Abu Dhabi Maritime Academy and Quincus for research and applications in maritime logistics.
  • Expanded cloud distribution through a new agreement with a leading hyperscaler serving millions of developers and advanced Oracle partnership by launching a joint beta program for hybrid quantum-AI applications.
  • Deepened U.S. government commitments by continuing to execute on DARPA QBI Stage B contract, actively discussing a Stage C scope of work, and participating in four winning proposals under Phase 1 of the Department of Energy’s Genesis Mission  
  • Advanced international deployments, with Helios assembly underway in Singapore ahead of spring 2027 commissioning and a Reimei system upgrade at RIKEN in Japan scheduled for completion this month.

Product Technology & Supply Chain:

  • Validated the Company’s leading path to universal, fully fault-tolerant quantum computing by 2029 with back-to-back accuracy world records on Helios using two codes within the same scalable, end-to-end logical architecture. Reached 99.9995% logical fidelity in October—within Apollo’s target range—with an error rate ten times lower than September’s record and 100 times lower than the best published result across other hardware modalities. Results also demonstrate Quantinuum’s significant overhead and scalability advantage.
  • Sol remains on track for 2H 2027, with full-scale control-system validation complete and integration and assembly targeted for Q1 2027, ahead of validation and tuning toward 100 logical qubits at a target logical error rate of 10⁻⁵.
  • Apollo remains on track for 2029, supported by design milestones, including validating that our cryogenic system can be deployed at the required scale.
  • Strengthened the manufacturing foundation for future systems through partnerships with GlobalFoundries, Infineon, Honeywell Aerospace and Monarch Quantum, and finalized the CHIPS R&D award as the only trapped-ion company selected.

Software:

  • Announced a multi-generational Nexus roadmap through Apollo, aligning application development and hybrid deployment with successive hardware generations to build what the Company believes will be the first developer platform designed for the fault-tolerant era.
  • Expanded fault-tolerant capabilities through a September Nexus release that extends Guppy tools for logical-qubit programming and supported error-correction encoding, reducing the need to rewrite applications for specific codes. Planned December release will expand responsive hybrid quantum-classical workflows, supported error-correction codes, and execution analytics for application optimization.
  • Accelerated Nexus adoption and usage, with adoption growing nearly 20% quarter-over-quarter to 215 organizations; total job submissions increased tenfold in the 12 months through August 2026 compared with the preceding 12-month period.

Ecosystem:  

  • Introduced QUOPS with Sandia National Laboratories and NVIDIA, benchmarking useful computational scale and speed. Quantinuum is building industry-wide alignment toward a common standard that supports customer comparisons and purchasing decisions.
  • Expanded the quantum user ecosystem, growing Q-Net to more than 800 members, adding eight startup partners and partnering with Singapore’s National Quantum Office to organize a global quantum challenge that attracted more than 200 submissions.

Financial Outlook
  • Raising full-year 2026 revenue outlook to $31 to $34 million, up from $28 to $32 million previously.  

Third Quarter 2026 Conference Call

Quantinuum will host a conference call at 5 PM Eastern time on Thursday, November 5, 2026, to discuss its results for the third quarter ended September 30, 2026, and provide a business update. The call will be available live via webcast here.

An archive replay of the webcast will be made available on the Quantinuum Investor Relations website following the call and will remain available for one year.  

Non-GAAP Financial Measures

To supplement Quantinuum’s condensed consolidated financial statements presented in accordance with U.S. generally accepted accounting principles (“GAAP”), the Company uses the following non-GAAP financial measures presented in this release: Adjusted Gross Profit, Adjusted Gross Margin, Adjusted Net Loss, fully distributed, Adjusted EBITDA, and Adjusted Net Loss Per Share, fully distributed.

Adjusted Gross Profit starts with GAAP gross profit and adds back equity compensation and related employer taxes attributable to cost of revenue and depreciation and amortization attributable to cost of revenue.

Adjusted Gross Margin is calculated as Adjusted Gross Profit divided by revenue, net.

Adjusted Net Loss, fully distributed starts with GAAP net loss on an as-converted basis, adjusts for equity compensation and related employer taxes, costs of the initial public offering and the transition to public company reporting, severance expense, the change in fair value of liability-classified warrants, and loss on disposal and write down of assets, and then applies an assumed statutory tax rate to the resulting adjusted pre-tax loss. No tax benefit is recognized in respect of losses subject to a full valuation allowance, and accordingly no tax benefit is reflected in the periods presented.

Adjusted EBITDA starts with Adjusted Net Loss, fully distributed, and further excludes income tax expense, interest income, net, depreciation, and amortization of acquired intangibles.

Adjusted Net Loss Per Share, fully distributed is calculated as Adjusted Net Loss, fully distributed, divided by adjusted shares, fully distributed, basic and diluted, comprising weighted-average Class A common shares outstanding and Common Units of Quantinuum Holdings.

Management believes these measures provide investors with additional information useful in evaluating the Company’s operating performance and trends across periods. Quantinuum’s results include large non-cash charges that management does not consider indicative of ongoing operating performance, principally stock-based compensation recognized on completion of the Reorganization and remeasurement of liability-classified warrants. Both are driven by accounting triggers and external inputs rather than operating activity. As an early commercial-stage business, Quantinuum’s period-to-period results also are affected by the timing of individual contracts. Measures that isolate underlying operating performance from non-cash and transition items help investors assess trends across periods.

Quantinuum’s Up-C structure means that GAAP net loss attributable to Quantinuum Inc. reflects only the Class A share of the economics. Presenting adjusted results on an as-converted, fully distributed basis describes the whole economic enterprise, which is how management assesses performance and how the business is managed. Management uses these measures for internal planning and forecasting, evaluating operating performance, and preparing budgets.

These non-GAAP financial measures are supplemental and are not prepared in accordance with GAAP. They are not intended to be considered in isolation or as a substitute for the most directly comparable financial information prepared in accordance with GAAP. Quantinuum’s non-GAAP measures may differ from similarly titled measures used by other companies and, therefore, may not be comparable. Investors should review the reconciliations and should not rely on any single financial measure to evaluate the Company’s business.

Each non-GAAP financial measure is reconciled to its most directly comparable GAAP financial measure in the tables at the end of this release.
